documents.proposal:
# Proposal: Make ADV reads disk-authoritative

Promote Epic `hardenTemporalReliability` shell #6 ("Make reads disk-authoritative — never block on a wedged workflow"). Make the durable disk projection the source of truth for reads; demote the Temporal workflow query to bounded, enrichment-only, circuit-broken.

## Changes

1. **Disk-first convergence.** `adv_epic_show`, `adv_change_list`, `adv_status` (incl. `view:health`), and `adv_change_show` resolve change/Epic/gate projections from the **durable disk projection** as source of truth. A wedged/poisoned/missing/unresponsive workflow degrades the read to **advisory** (surface a bounded `_recovery`/staleness note) but never fails or hangs it.
2. **Extend present-but-unresponsive handling.** The existing fast-fallback (currently `missing_workflow`-only) gains a **bounded per-member query timeout + circuit-breaker** so a present-but-wedged workflow trips to the disk projection instead of hanging (closes the gap that made `addDependencyAwareResume` hang `adv_change_show`).
3. **`adv_status` health correctness.** The `resumeProjection`/convergence phase must not consume the health budget; temporal probes must actually run and be reported (kill the false `"server down"` default caused by execution cutoff).
4. **Worktree-cleanup disk-only fallback (#248).** Include the disk-only path so worktree cleanup never times out on an unreachable workflow.
5. **Projection reconciliation for archived/missing children.** With disk-first reads, the residual `projection_missing`/stale archived cohort (`gateMutationSuccessDisk`, `slimMutationToolSurface`, `tightenToolOutputDefaults`, `fixWorktreeReuseRegistration`, `addDependencyAwareResume`) converges to terminal projection without manual `adv_archive_purge`.

## Outcome / acceptance direction

- The 2026-07-23 reproduction (one archived wedged member hanging `adv_epic_show`/`adv_change_list`/`adv_status`) no longer hangs; reads return with at most an advisory staleness marker.
- A poisoned/wedged/missing child workflow never blocks an epic/list/status/show read.
- `adv_status view:health` reports real probe results, not a budget-starved default.
- Regression: a test that registers/inserts an unresponsive workflow member and asserts the read returns (advisory) within budget.

## Mapping

- Epic `hardenTemporalReliability` invariant #1 (primary). Sibling/prerequisite to invariant #4 (shell #16, write/archive durability).
- Related issues: #198 (disk-projection recovery defeated by live wedged workflow), #248 (worktree cleanup times out), #253 (archive poisoned recovery when workflow missing).
documents.problemStatement:
# Problem: ADV read paths block on Temporal workflow queries

## Symptom (live reproduction, 2026-07-23 `/adv-coordinate`)

ADV read tools — `adv_epic_show`, `adv_change_list`, `adv_status`, `adv_change_show` — converge change/Epic projections by issuing **per-member Temporal workflow state queries as a read precondition**, with no per-member query timeout or circuit-breaker inside the read's single tool deadline. A single present-but-unresponsive child workflow query blocks past the deadline → `ToolExecutionTimeout` (10000ms) → **the entire read fails as a unit**, even though:

- the Temporal worker/server is healthy (`adv_doctor` liveness probe = all-green), and
- every other member converges fine.

## Evidence (adv-temporal-repair triage, 2026-07-23)

- `adv_epic_show` on `hardenTemporalReliability` **AND** `adv_change_list` both timed out (10000ms) ~1s after `adv_doctor` reported `server_alive/worker_alive/queue_serviceable/search_attributes_ok` all true, zero fixes.
- Blocking member isolated: `addDependencyAwareResume` (archived; workflow present-but-unresponsive query handler). `adv_archive_purge` (workflow-only) reconciled it → `workflowTerminated:true`, **`alreadyTerminated:true`** — i.e. the workflow had actually **completed**; only the convergence projection was stale, yet the read path kept querying it and hanging.
- `adv_change_show` is only **partially** disk-first: fast-fallback to disk when a workflow is **missing** (`_recovery.reason:"missing_workflow"`), but still issues the query and **hangs** when a workflow is **present-but-wedged**. So "disk-first" today = "disk-fallback-on-404", not true disk-authoritative.
- `adv_status view:health` degrades the same way: its `resumeProjection` convergence phase ate the 8s response budget (13271ms), so the real temporal probes were cut (`not_admitted: execution cutoff`) and health fell back to a default `"Temporal: server down ✗"` string — a **false outage**, not a measurement.
- Residual cohort: even with a healthy worker, multiple **archived** children (`gateMutationSuccessDisk`, `slimMutationToolSurface`, `tightenToolOutputDefaults`, `fixWorktreeReuseRegistration`) stay `projection_missing`/stale because **no force-flip tool exists** — convergence must become disk-first to resolve them without manual operator purges.

## Why it matters

This violates Epic `hardenTemporalReliability` **invariant #1** ("a wedged/poisoned/missing/unresponsive workflow never blocks a read"). It is the recurring **"the system is wedged during ordinary reads/archives/cleanup"** failure mode the Epic exists to end. Operators are forced into narrow recovery tools (`adv_archive_purge`, `adv_change_workflow_terminate`) for what should be a transparent read.

## Root cause

Read-path convergence treats the Temporal workflow query as authoritative and the disk projection as a fallback, inverting the intended invariant. There is no bounded per-member query timeout and no circuit-breaker, so one slow/dead member holds the whole read hostage.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- Determinism discipline / patch lifecycle (invariant #2, separate shell #8).
- Retiring the recovery-tool sprawl (invariant #3, entry #9 shipped).
- False-negative durability guards on the **write/archive** path (invariant #4, shell #16) — though disk-authoritative reads are a prerequisite/sibling.
documents.agreement:
# Agreement: Make reads disk-authoritative

## Objectives
1. ADV read tools (`adv_epic_show`, `adv_change_list`, `adv_status` incl. `view:health`, `adv_change_show`) resolve change/Epic/gate projections from the **durable disk projection as source of truth**.
2. The Temporal workflow query is **enrichment-only**, bounded by a per-member query timeout + per-request **circuit-breaker** — never a read precondition.
3. A wedged/poisoned/missing/unresponsive workflow **degrades the read to advisory** (`_recovery` marker), never fails or hangs it.
4. `adv_status view:health` reports real probe results, not a budget-starved false `"Temporal: server down"` default.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A present-but-unresponsive workflow member does not exceed the read budget; the read returns within `perMemberCap + ε` carrying `_recovery.reason === "workflow_unresponsive"` (regression test `convergent-read-disk-authoritative.test.ts` + `bounded-read-deadline.test.ts` extension).
- AC2: After K=3 consecutive unresponsive members, the circuit-breaker short-circuits remaining per-member queries to disk+advisory (list-resolved CB test in `index.test.ts`).
- AC3: Epic-side read (`epics.get` / `queryEpicState`) threads a read deadline and returns a disk projection + advisory on an unresponsive Epic workflow instead of hanging (epics.test.ts).
- AC4: `appendResumeProjectionRecommendations` uses bounded concurrency (`mapWithConcurrency(8)`), so one hung member cannot peg the phase (status-enrich.test.ts).
- AC5: A read-path timeout does NOT trigger the false `"Temporal: server down"` health fallback (`probe_degraded`) (status-health.test.ts, health-probe-cache.test.ts).
- AC6 (live): post-deploy+restart, `adv_epic_show` / `adv_change_list` / `adv_doctor` return fast with zero `ToolExecutionTimeout` — **VERIFIED 2026-07-23** (the wedge that motivated this change is resolved).

## Constraints
- Fix surface is **tool-handler/storage layer only**; `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts` must NOT be touched (replay-deterministic; boundary tests `workflow-bundle-boundary.test.ts` + `workflow-bundle-imports.test.ts` enforce it cannot reach storage/tools).
- **Mutation-safety preserved**: the new `workflow_unresponsive` recovery reason authorizes read-only disk fallback ONLY — it NEVER authorizes re-seed/mutation (mirrors `poisoned_history`, NOT `missing_workflow`'s reseed path).
- `pnpm run check` (schemas/typecheck/lint/format) + `pnpm run build` must stay green; if Zod schemas changed, `pnpm run schemas:generate` keeps `schemas:check` green.

## Avoidances
- Do not alter query semantics for healthy/responsive workflows (enrichment must still enrich when fast).
- Do not regress the existing `listResolvedChanges` disk-first fast path.
- Do not widen the worker-bundle import graph (keep workflows.ts unreachable from the change).
- No hot-reload assumption: change takes effect only after build + deploy + OpenCode restart.
documents.design:
# Design: Make reads disk-authoritative

## Architecture decision
**Invert the read-path authority.** Today the Temporal workflow query is the source of truth and the disk projection is a fallback (only on `missing_workflow`). The fix makes the **durable disk projection the source of truth** and demotes the workflow query to **bounded, enrichment-only** with a per-request circuit-breaker. This realizes Epic `hardenTemporalReliability` invariant #1.

## Two independent query surfaces
1. **Change-side (single shared kernel):** `getTemporalChange` (`storage/store-temporal/index.ts:778`). Fixing this one function benefits `adv_change_show`, the per-member legs of `adv_change_list`, and the `resumeProjection` phase.
2. **Epic-side (separate path):** `queryEpicState` / `tryQueryEpicState` / `epics.get` (`storage/store-temporal/epics.ts`). Has no deadline context today; fixed independently with parity to the change-side pattern.

## Implementation strategy (shipped)

### Recovery taxonomy extension (`temporal/recovery-classification.ts`)
- Add `workflow_unresponsive` to `RECOVERY_REASONS` (and thus to `ProjectionRecoveryReason = Exclude<RecoveryReason,"query_failed">`, authorizing disk fallback).
- `recoveryReasonFromError` classifies `TemporalQueryTimeout` / timeout-message errors as `workflow_unresponsive`.
- **LBP/safety:** `workflow_unresponsive` mirrors `poisoned_history` — read-only disk fallback, **NEVER** authorizes re-seed/mutation. Distinct from `missing_workflow`'s reseed path. This preserves the mutation-safety invariant (P33): the disk projection may be stale, so it must not drive writes.

### Per-request circuit-breaker (`storage/store-temporal/read-context.ts`)
- Extend `TemporalReadContext` with `unresponsiveCount`, `circuitBreakerTripped`, and `recordResponsive()`/`recordUnresponsive()`/`isCircuitBreakerTripped()`.
- After K=3 consecutive unresponsive members, short-circuit remaining per-member queries to disk+advisory. Reuses the existing per-request context (per the recon's recommendation) so the CB is scoped to one read, not global state.
- Resets the streak on any responsive member (transient slowness doesn't permanently trip).

### Disk-first two-leg restructure (`getTemporalChange`)
- Mirror the proven `loadCandidate` pattern (`index.ts:1335-1509`): **Leg A** race `legacy.changes.get(changeId)` (disk) against the remaining deadline; **Leg B** Temporal `changeStateQuery` as enrichment-only at a lowered per-member cap.
- Per-member cap lowered `QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` 5000→1500ms (gives headroom: 1500ms × 3 CB-trip ≈ 4.5s of the 8s aggregate, leaving budget for disk reads).
- CB-tripped or unresponsive → `withProjectionRecovery(change,"disk","workflow_unresponsive")` and return disk projection. `loadTerminalProjection` short-circuit preserved.

### Epic parity (`epics.ts`)
- Thread `TemporalReadContext` (deadline) through `queryEpicState`/`tryQueryEpicState`/`get`.
- Add a disk-first leg (analogous to `loadTerminalProjection`); on unresponsive → typed advisory + disk projection. `tryQueryEpicState` no longer only catches `isWorkflowNotFoundError`.

### `adv_status` resumeProjection + health
- `appendResumeProjectionRecommendations` (`tools/status-enrich.ts`): sequential `for` loop → `mapWithConcurrency(8)` (matches `tools/resume-projection.ts:77`).
- Health false-down guard: add `probe_degraded` to `TemporalHealth`; `buildTemporalHealthFallback` distinguishes timeout (→ `server_alive:true, probe_degraded:true`) from genuine unreachability (→ false "server down"). `isTemporalHealthUsable` treats degraded as usable. Kills the budget-starved false outage.

## LBP / structural-correctness notes
- The fix is structural (typed recovery reason + per-request CB state machine + deadline-bounded queries), not heuristic. Heuristics (timeout detection regex) are isolated to classification and guarded by the typed reason.
- Mutation-safety is enforced by the type system: `ProjectionRecoveryReason` excludes `query_failed`; `workflow_unresponsive` is in the projection-safe set but its handler path is read-only by construction (no reseed call).

## Replay verdict
**NOT replay-sensitive.** All changed code is in `storage/store-temporal/**` and `tools/**`. `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts` is untouched; `workflow-bundle-boundary.test.ts` + `workflow-bundle-imports.test.ts` enforce it cannot transitively reach the changed files. No replay-determinism harness changes needed.

## Independent validation
The adv-tron reconnaissance (2026-07-23, 31 evidence files) served as the independent architectural validation: confirmed the single-shared-kernel vs separate-epic-path split, the no-circuit-breaker gap, the absent taxonomy reason, and the replay-safety verdict. (Fast-track: work already shipped live; formal adv-researcher design validator waived per user fast-track approval, with recon as the evidence substitute.)
documents.executiveSummary:
# Executive Summary: Make reads disk-authoritative

## Outcome
ADV read tools (`adv_epic_show`, `adv_epic_list`, `adv_change_list`, `adv_change_show`, `adv_status`) no longer hang when a child workflow is wedged, poisoned, missing, or unresponsive. Reads resolve from the durable disk projection as source of truth; the Temporal workflow query is bounded, enrichment-only, and circuit-broken. A wedged member degrades the read to an advisory marker instead of failing or hanging the whole read.

## Why it matters
This ends the recurring "the system is wedged during ordinary reads/archives/cleanup" failure class — Epic `hardenTemporalReliability` invariant #1. Operators no longer need manual recovery tools (`adv_archive_purge`, `adv_change_workflow_terminate`) to unblock ordinary reads; one wedged workflow can't hold an entire epic/list/status read hostage.

## What was delivered
- `workflow_unresponsive` recovery reason (read-only disk fallback; NEVER authorizes re-seed/mutation — mutation-safe).
- Per-request circuit-breaker on `TemporalReadContext` (K=3 consecutive unresponsive → short-circuit).
- Change-side `getTemporalChange` restructured to disk-first two-leg; query demoted to bounded enrichment (1500ms cap).
- `adv_status view:health` distinguishes read-timeout (`probe_degraded`) from genuine unreachability — kills the false "Temporal: server down" default.
- Lowered per-member cap 5000→1500ms for aggregate-budget headroom.

## Verification
- `pnpm run check` + `pnpm run build` green; 255+ tests pass including new regressions (unresponsive member → advisory within budget; CB trip after K=3).
- **Live verification (2026-07-23):** post-deploy+restart, `adv_epic_show`/`adv_epic_list`/`adv_change_list`/`adv_doctor` all return fast, zero `ToolExecutionTimeout` — the motivating wedge is resolved.
- Replay-safe: `workflows.ts` untouched; boundary tests enforce the fix surface can't reach it.

## Risks / follow-ups
- **epic-list/show CB gap (review finding epic-read-1)** — the initial ship covered `epics.get` + change-side; the epic convergence loop was unprotected. **Shipped** via fast-follow `addEpicListCircuitBreaker` (commit 7de2cd0b, live) — epic reads now also unblocked.
- **`probe_degraded` inverse concern (review finding health-guard-1)** — a timeout reports alive, which could mask a real outage. Tracked as `fixHealthDegradedAlive` (lower-urgency follow-up).
- Disk-projection write-lag tolerated via the two-leg pattern; `workflow_unresponsive` is deliberately non-authoritative for writes.

## Release readiness
Code merged to trunk (`1879fb64`), deployed (bundle gen verified), restarted, verified live. Safe to release — strictly improves read resilience; no mutation-path authority changes.
